assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only one we know with liquid water and life!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition

It only provides a single fact about Earth, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why is Earth called the blue planet?

Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only one we know with liquid water and life! That's why it's the blue planet.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na asul na planeta ang Daigdig?

Ang Daigdig ay ang ikatlong planeta mula sa Araw at ang tanging may tubig at buhay! Kaya naman tinatawag itong asul na planeta.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag nga asul nga planeta ang Kalibotan?

Ang Kalibotan mao ang ikatulong planeta gikan sa Adlaw ug ang bugtong adunay tubig ug kinabuhi! Busa gitawag kining asul nga planeta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth travels about 30 kilometers every second as it orbits the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states Earth's orbital speed. It does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon model or explaining seasons, star patterns, or eclipses, which are the actions and effects required by G6-E-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth travels about 30 kilometers every second as it orbits the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives one fact about Earth's motion but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or address their main features and composition as required by G5-E-11.

copy.en:
How fast does Earth travel around the Sun?

Very fast! Earth travels about 30 kilometers every second as it orbits the Sun, yet we do not feel this motion at all.
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis ang paglakbay ng Earth sa Araw?

Napakabilis! Umiikot ang Earth sa Araw nang mga 30 kilometro kada segundo, pero hindi natin nararamdaman ang paggalaw na ito.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadpas ang pagbiyahe sa Earth palibot sa Adlaw?

Paspas kaayo! Molibot ang Earth sa Adlaw nga mga 30 ka kilometro matag segundo, apan dili gyud nato mabati kining paglihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stars aren't just white! They can be red, yellow, or blue.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses star colors and temperature, mentioning the Sun, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their features, or composition.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses 'heat' loosely to mean temperature and does not explain the difference between heat and temperature as concepts.

copy.en: Stars aren't just white! They can be red, yellow, or blue. Color shows heat: red is coolest, blue is hottest, and our yellow-white Sun is right in the middle!
copy.tl: Hindi puti lang ang bituin! Pula, dilaw, o asul. Ang kulay ay nagpapakita ng init: pula ang pinakamalamig, asul ang pinakamainit, at ang dilaw-puti nating Araw ay nasa gitna!
copy.bis: Dili puti lang ang bituon! Pula, dalag, o asul. Kolor nagpakita sa kainit: pula pinakabugnaw, asul pinakainit, ug dalag-puti natong Adlaw naa sa tunga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is the third planet from the Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states Earth's ordinal position from the Sun. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name other major celestial objects, or give their main features and composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is our planet's special number order from the Sun?

Earth is the third planet from the Sun! It's our special spot in the Solar System.
copy.tl:
Ano ang espesyal na pagkakasunod-sunod ng planeta natin mula sa Araw?

Ang Earth ang ikatlong planeta mula sa Araw! Ito ang ating espesyal na lugar sa Solar System.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang espesyal nga sunod-sunod sa atong planeta gikan sa Adlaw?

Ang Earth mao ang ikatulo nga planeta gikan sa Adlaw! Kini ang atong espesyal nga dapit sa Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines has no winter or four seasons because it's near the equator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why the Philippines lacks four seasons, but the competency requires describing the different seasons in the Philippines (e.g., wet and dry) and suggesting appropriate activities. The card does not describe any actual Philippine seasons or activities, so it only touches the same broad topic without directly supporting the required skill.

copy.en: The Philippines has no winter or four seasons because it's near the equator! There, the Sun's warmth stays almost the same all year, keeping our country tropical and warm.
copy.tl: Walang winter o apat na panahon ang Pilipinas dahil malapit tayo sa ekwador! Dito, halos pantay ang init ng Araw buong taon, kaya palagi tayong tropical at mainit.
copy.bis: Walay winter o upat ka panahon ang Pilipinas tungod kay duol mi sa ekwador! Dinhi, halos managsama ang kainit sa Adlaw tibuok tuig, mao nga tropical ug init kanunay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One year on Earth lasts about 365 days, the time it takes Earth to travel once around the Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Earth's orbital period, but the competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, naming major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition. The card does not address the solar system's structure or other celestial objects, so it only shares vocabulary (Earth, Sun) without directly supporting the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One year on Earth lasts about 365 days, the time it takes Earth to travel once around the Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses

It is background knowledge about Earth's revolution but not direct support for this competency.

copy.en:
How long is one year on Earth?

One year on Earth lasts about 365 days, the time it takes Earth to travel once around the Sun!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal ang isang taon sa Mundo?

Ang isang taon sa Mundo ay tumatagal ng halos 365 araw, ang oras na kailangan para makapaglibot ang Mundo sa Araw nang isang beses!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang usa ka tuig sa Yuta?

Ang usa ka tuig sa Yuta motagal ug mga 365 ka adlaw, ang panahon nga gikinahanglan aron makalibot ang Yuta sa Adlaw sa makausa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the safest thing to do is always prepare in advance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: refer to the local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that earthquakes cannot be predicted and advises general preparation. It does not refer to local disaster readiness plans or demonstrate specific actions during and after an earthquake, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Can scientists predict exactly when an earthquake will happen?

No scientist can predict the exact day and time of an earthquake yet! That is why the safest thing to do is always prepare in advance.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang hulaan ng mga siyentipiko kung kailan eksaktong magkakaroon ng lindol?

Hindi pa kayang hulaan ng kahit sinong siyentipiko ang eksaktong araw at oras ng lindol! Kaya ang pinakaligtas na gawin ay laging maghanda nang maaga.
copy.bis:
Makatagna ba ang mga siyentista kung kanus-a eksakto ang linog?

Wala pay siyentista nga makatagna sa eksaktong adlaw ug oras sa linog! Mao nga ang pinakaluwas nga buhaton mao ang kanunay nga pagpangandam og sayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two different particle motions and two different speeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares P-waves and S-waves in an earthquake, which are classic examples of longitudinal and transverse waves, but it never names the wave types as longitudinal or transverse, nor does it describe the distinguishing particle motion (parallel vs perpendicular) or other similarities/differences. It only states that they have different particle motions and speeds, which is too vague to directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
How do P-waves and S-waves compare in one earthquake?

They make a perfect contrast! Same event and rock, but they have two different particle motions and two different speeds.
copy.tl:
Paano magkumpara ang P-waves at S-waves sa isang lindol?

Magandang contrast! Parehong pangyayari at bato, pero may dalawang magkaibang particle motions at dalawang magkaibang bilis.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkumpara ang P-waves ug S-waves sa usa ka linog?

Maayong contrast! Parehas nga panghitabo ug bato, apan adunay duha ka lahi nga particle motions ug duha ka lahi nga kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Part of earthquake preparedness! This keeps them from toppling over and hurting someone when the ground shakes.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: refer to the local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why to fasten furniture as an earthquake preparedness measure, but the competency requires referring to local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake. The card does not address local plans or actions during/after an earthquake; it is only a general safety tip related to earthquake preparedness.

copy.en:
Why should we fasten tall cabinets and shelves to the wall?

Part of earthquake preparedness! This keeps them from toppling over and hurting someone when the ground shakes.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat nating ikabit ang matataas na aparador at istante sa pader?

Bahagi ito ng paghahanda sa lindol! Para hindi sila matumba at makasakit kapag yumanig ang lupa.
copy.bis:
Nganong dapat nato kabiton ang habog nga mga aparador ug estante sa bungbong?

Kabahin kini sa pagpangandam sa linog! Aron dili kini matumba ug makadaot kon mouyog ang yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it breathes through its moist, damp skin instead!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physiological mechanism (breathing through skin) but does not describe an example of animals changing to better suit their environment, nor does it involve using secondary sources. It shares the broad topic of animals but does not directly support the adaptation/evolution competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An earthworm doesn't have lungs — it breathes through its moist, damp skin instead!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about describing how human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The card is about an earthworm's respiration, not a human body system. It does not describe any human system, so it is only related by the general concept of breathing.

copy.en:
How does an earthworm breathe?

An earthworm doesn't have lungs — it breathes through its moist, damp skin instead!
copy.tl:
Paano humihinga ang bulate?

Walang baga ang bulate — sa halip, humihinga ito sa pamamagitan ng basa nitong balat!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagginhawa sa wati?

Wala'y baga ang wati — hinuon, manginhawa kini pinaagi sa iyang basa nga panit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A worm has no teeth — it swallows tiny grains of sand that stay in its gut and uses them to crush food as it passes through!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a worm's gut and sand-grit digestion, but does not identify or describe the human digestive system parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It shares the broad topic of digestion but provides no direct support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A worm has no teeth — it swallows tiny grains of sand that stay in its gut and uses them to crush food as it passes through!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). The card discusses a worm's digestive mechanism, not any human body system, so it does not directly support the required content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A worm has no teeth — it swallows tiny grains of sand that stay in its gut and uses them to crush food as it passes through!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks for examples of animals that have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. The card describes a behavioral/structural feeding adaptation (using grit to grind food) but does not frame it as an evolutionary adaptation to the environment, nor does it mention mimicry or camouflage. It is only tangentially related to adaptation.

copy.en:
How does a worm chew without teeth?

A worm has no teeth — it swallows tiny grains of sand that stay in its gut and uses them to crush food as it passes through!
copy.tl:
Paano dinudurog ng bulate ang pagkain kahit walang ngipin?

Walang ngipin ang bulate — lumululon ito ng maliliit na butil ng buhangin na nananatili sa tiyan nito, at ginagamit para gilingin ang pagkain habang dumadaan sa katawan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdugmok sa wati sa pagkaon kon walay ngipon?

Walay ngipon ang wati — magtulon kini og gagmayng lugas sa balas nga magpabilin sa tiyan, ug gamiton kini aron galingon ang pagkaon samtang moagi sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most adult echinoderms, like sea stars and sea urchins, have five-part radial symmetry
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: five-part radial symmetry — but sea cucumbers are long-shaped
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Five-part symmetry is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en: Most adult echinoderms, like sea stars and sea urchins, have five-part radial symmetry — but sea cucumbers are long-shaped, though their insides are still arranged in five parts.
copy.tl: Karamihan ng mga adult echinoderm, tulad ng sea star at sea urchin, ay may limang-bahaging radial symmetry — pero ang sea cucumber ay mahaba ang hugis, kahit nakaayos pa rin sa lima ang laman nito.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa hamtong nga echinoderms, sama sa sea star ug sea urchin, adunay lima ka bahin nga radial symmetry — apan ang sea cucumber pahaba ang hulma, bisan ang sulod niini gibahin gihapon sa lima.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Starfish and sea urchins have bodies split into five matching parts arranged around the center
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Five-fold symmetry is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: called five-fold radial symmetry
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

copy.en:
What body pattern do starfish share?

Starfish and sea urchins have bodies split into five matching parts arranged around the center — called five-fold radial symmetry.
copy.tl:
Anong pattern ang katawan ng starfish?

Ang katawan ng starfish at tihik ay hati sa limang magkaparehong bahagi na nakaayos paikot sa gitna — tinatawag itong limang-bahaging simetriya.
copy.bis:
Unsang porma ang lawas sa starfish?

Ang lawas sa starfish ug tihik gibahin sa lima ka managsama nga bahin nga gihan-ay palibot sa tunga — gitawag kini og lima-ka-bahin nga radial symmetry.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: both belong to a group of spiny-skinned sea animals called echinoderms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Echinoderm kinship is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a group of spiny-skinned sea animals called echinoderms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

copy.en: The starfish and the sea urchin are actually relatives — both belong to a group of spiny-skinned sea animals called echinoderms.
copy.tl: Magkamag-anak pala ang starfish at ang tihik — parehong kabilang sila sa grupo ng mga hayop-dagat na may matinik na balat, ang echinoderm.
copy.bis: Magparyente diay ang starfish ug ang tihik — pareho sila sakop sa grupo sa mga mananap-dagat nga adunay tunokon nga panit, ang echinoderm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By listening to echoes, bats and dolphins can tell how close, how big, and what shape an object is!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an ability (echolocation) of bats and dolphins but does not frame it as a change or adaptation to better suit their environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or evolutionary change. It only states a current capability, so it does not directly support the competency's skill of describing how animals have changed to suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By listening to echoes, bats and dolphins can tell how close, how big, and what shape an object is!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves sound (echoes) and hearing, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It focuses on the use of echoes for perception by animals, not on the production or transfer of sound, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: By listening to echoes, bats and dolphins can tell how close, how big, and what shape an object is!
copy.tl: Sa pakikinig sa alingawngaw, nalalaman ng paniki at lumba-lumba kung gaano kalapit, kalaki, at anong hugis ang isang bagay!
copy.bis: Pinaagi sa pagpaminaw sa alingawngaw, mahibal-an sa kabog ug lumba-lumba kon unsa kaduol, kadako, ug unsa nga porma ang usa ka butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when an allele's frequency changes over time, it's a sign evolution is happening
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses allele frequency change as evidence of evolution, but does not address the specific concepts listed in the competency (variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation). It is only broadly related to evolution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when an allele's frequency changes over time, it's a sign evolution is happening
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions evolution but does not describe natural selection as the primary mechanism. It focuses on allele frequency change as a sign of evolution, not on natural selection itself.

copy.en:
How do scientists tell evolution is happening?

By studying allele frequency in a population -- when an allele's frequency changes over time, it's a sign evolution is happening.
copy.tl:
Paano nasusukat ng siyentipiko na may ebolusyon?

Sa pag-aaral ng frequency ng allele sa isang populasyon -- kapag nagbago ito sa paglipas ng panahon, tanda itong may ebolusyong nagaganap.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-ila sa siyentista nga adunay ebolusyon?

Pinaagi sa pagtuon sa frequency sa allele sa usa ka populasyon -- kon mausab kini sa paglabay sa panahon, timaan kini nga adunay ebolusyon nga nagakahitabo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People often say Eduardo San Juan made the moon buggy, but the lunar rover was actually built by many NASA engineers together!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Eduardo San Juan and the moon buggy, but it does not identify his invention; it corrects a common misconception, stating the rover was built by many NASA engineers. It does not provide information needed to identify a scientist and their invention, so it is only related to the topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People often say Eduardo San Juan made the moon buggy, but the lunar rover was actually built by many NASA engineers together!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use information from home or local community to identify a science invention or explain its impact on everyday life. It only discusses a claim about the moon buggy's origin, which is not tied to local community or everyday impact.

copy.en: People often say Eduardo San Juan made the moon buggy, but the lunar rover was actually built by many NASA engineers together!
copy.tl: Madalas sabihin na si Eduardo San Juan ang gumawa ng moon buggy, pero ang lunar rover ay ginawa ng maraming NASA engineers nang magkakasama!
copy.bis: Kasagaran giingon nga si Eduardo San Juan ang naghimo sa moon buggy, apan ang tinuod, ang lunar rover gihimo sa daghang NASA engineers nga nagtinabangay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In females, meiosis produces one large egg cell and three tiny polar bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the female reproductive system as ovaries, uterus, and vagina and those of the male reproductive system as the prostate, testis, and penis and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses meiosis and egg/polar body formation, but G5-L-3 requires identifying and describing the parts of the female reproductive system (ovaries, uterus, vagina) and male reproductive system (prostate, testis, penis). The card does not mention any of these organs or their functions, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: In females, meiosis produces one large egg cell and three tiny polar bodies that are not used in humans.
copy.tl: Sa mga babae, ang meiosis ay gumagawa ng isang malaking egg cell at tatlong maliliit na polar bodies na hindi ginagamit sa tao.
copy.bis: Sa mga babaye, ang meiosis naghimo ug usa ka dako nga itlog nga cell ug tulo ka gagmay nga polar bodies nga dili gamiton sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The white egret is a long-legged, long-necked bird often seen in rice fields and ponds, hunting for fish and insects.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card names two outer body parts (legs, neck) and mentions hunting, but it does not describe the role of these parts in movement or gathering food. It does not explicitly connect the long legs to wading or the long neck to catching prey, so it does not directly teach the competency's skill of identifying the role of body parts.

copy.en: The white egret is a long-legged, long-necked bird often seen in rice fields and ponds, hunting for fish and insects.
copy.tl: Ang puting tagak ay isang ibong may mahabang paa at leeg na kadalasang nakikita sa mga palayan at lawa, naghahanap ng isda at insekto.
copy.bis: Ang puti nga tagak usa ka langgam nga adunay tag-as nga tiil ug liog nga kasagarang makita sa kahumayan ug linaw, nangita og isda ug insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: press its head against the attacker to give a stronger shock
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the eel's head as a body part, but the role described is delivering a stronger shock for defense, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency. It does not directly support observing/describing outer body parts for movement or food gathering.

copy.en:
Can an electric eel attack by jumping?

Yes! When threatened, it can leap up and press its head against the attacker to give a stronger shock.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang lumukso ng electric eel?

Oo! Kapag nanganganib, lumulukso ito paitaas at idinidikit ang ulo sa kalaban para mas malakas ang shock.
copy.bis:
Makalukso ba ang electric eel?

Oo! Kon naa'y peligro, molukso kini pataas ug ipaduol ang ulo sa kaaway aron mas kusog ang shock.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel makes electricity to stun its prey.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an electric eel's ability to produce electricity to stun prey, but does not address how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor mimicry or camouflage. It is only tangentially related to animal adaptations.

copy.en:
Can an eel make electricity?

Yes! The electric eel makes electricity to stun its prey.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang gumawa ng kuryente ng isang eel?

Oo! Ang electric eel ay nakakagawa ng kuryente para tumbahin ang kanyang biktima.
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba og koryente ang eel?

Oo! Ang electric eel makahimo og koryente aron matumba ang iyang biktima.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel, living in South American rivers, can release a shock strong enough to knock down a big animal or protect itself.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a striking ability of the electric eel but does not mention adaptation, change, or environmental suitability, nor does it use secondary sources. It shares the broad topic of animal traits but does not directly support the competency about animals changing to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electric eel, living in South American rivers, can release a shock strong enough to knock down a big animal or protect itself.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the electric eel lives in rivers (aquatic habitat) but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat, and the electric eel is not a Philippine animal. The format-required activity is absent, so this is at most related_only.

copy.en:
What is one of the strongest electric animals?

The electric eel, living in South American rivers, can release a shock strong enough to knock down a big animal or protect itself.
copy.tl:
Ano ang isa sa pinakamalakas na electric na hayop?

Ang electric eel, na nakatira sa mga ilog ng South America, ay kayang magpalabas ng kuryenteng sapat para patumbahin ang malaking hayop o protektahan ang sarili.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang usa sa pinakakusog nga electric nga mananap?

Ang electric eel, nga nagpuyo sa mga suba sa South America, makahimo og kuryente nga igo aron matumba ang dako nga mananap o mapanalipdan ang iyang kaugalingon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electricity travels through water more easily than air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that water conducts electricity better than air, which touches on the concept of conductors, but it does not support designing or constructing a simple circuit, nor does it guide identifying materials that will and will not conduct electricity. It is background knowledge about conductivity, not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do electric eel shocks work so well in water?

Electricity travels through water more easily than air — that's why an electric eel's shock can spread through the water and reach its prey before even touching it.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabisa ang kuryente ng electric eel sa tubig?

Mas madaling dumaan ang kuryente sa tubig kaysa sa hangin — kaya kayang kumalat ang kuryente ng electric eel sa tubig para tamaan ang biktima kahit hindi pa ito nahahawakan.
copy.bis:
Nganong epektibo ang kuryente sa electric eel sa tubig?

Mas sayon moagi ang kuryente sa tubig kaysa sa hangin — mao nga makakatap ang kuryente sa electric eel sa tubig aron makaabot sa biktima bisan wala pa kini mahikap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electric animals don't just use their shocks for defense — they also use them to hunt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes using electric shocks to stun prey for food, but it does not mention or describe any outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and food gathering. It shares the broad topic of animals gathering food but gives no direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sudden jolt stuns small fish so they can be caught easily.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavior (using electric shocks to hunt) but does not describe how animals have changed over time to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not address adaptation or evolutionary change, so it is only related to the general topic of animal survival strategies.

copy.en: Electric animals don't just use their shocks for defense — they also use them to hunt. A sudden jolt stuns small fish so they can be caught easily.
copy.tl: Hindi lang panlaban ang kuryente ng mga hayop — ginagamit din ito para manghuli. Pinapatulala ng biglang kuryente ang maliliit na isda para madaling mahuli.
copy.bis: Dili lang panalipod ang kuryente sa mga mananap — gigamit usab kini sa pagpangita og pagkaon. Ang kalit nga kuryente makapahunong sa gagmayng isda aron sayon madakpan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Electromagnets show us that electricity and magnetism are connected—and this connection is called electromagnetism!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines electromagnetism as the connection between electricity and magnetism. It does not instruct how to make a simple electromagnet, nor does it guide observation or recording of its properties, which are the actions required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is electromagnetism?

Electromagnets show us that electricity and magnetism are connected—and this connection is called electromagnetism!
copy.tl:
Ano ang elektromagnetismo?

Ipinapakita ng elektromagnet na magkaugnay ang elektrisidad at magnetismo—at ang tawag dito ay elektromagnetismo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang elektromagnetismo?

Nagpakita ang elektromagnet nga magkadugtong ang elektrisidad ug magnetismo—ug kini nga koneksyon gitawag ug elektromagnetismo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An integrated circuit (IC) or microchip is a tiny silicon piece with millions of transistors.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes integrated circuits and transistors but does not address current, voltage, resistance, or series/parallel circuits. It shares the broad electronics topic but provides no instructional support for the competency's investigation of circuit relationships.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An integrated circuit (IC) or microchip is a tiny silicon piece with millions of transistors.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions transistors and microchips but does not explain electricity as a flow of electrons or discuss safe handling of electricity. It is only tangentially related to the competency's core concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These tiny ICs power our smartphones, computers, and almost all modern devices!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a science invention (the integrated circuit) and notes its impact on everyday devices, but it does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the impact in the depth required by the competency. It is a general statement rather than a guided identification/explanation activity.

copy.en: An integrated circuit (IC) or microchip is a tiny silicon piece with millions of transistors. These tiny ICs power our smartphones, computers, and almost all modern devices!
copy.tl: Ang integrated circuit (IC) o microchip ay isang maliit na piraso ng silicon na may milyun-milyong transistors. Pinapagana ng mga IC na ito ang ating smartphones, computers, at halos lahat ng modernong device!
copy.bis: Ang integrated circuit (IC) o microchip usa ka gagmay nga piraso sa silicon nga adunay milyon-milyong transistors. Gipagana sa mga IC ang atong smartphones, computers, ug halos tanan nga modernong device!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oganesson, also known as element 118, is the last and heaviest element on the periodic table!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies oganesson (element 118), a synthetic superheavy element, but the competency targets the first 20 or several common elements. Oganesson is neither among the first 20 nor a common element, so the card does not directly support the skill of identifying names and symbols of those elements.

copy.en: Oganesson, also known as element 118, is the last and heaviest element on the periodic table!
copy.tl: Ang oganesson, nga kilala rin bilang element 118, ang pinakahuli at pinakamabigat na elemento sa periodic table!
copy.bis: Ang oganesson, nga nailhan usab nga element 118, mao ang ulahi ug pinakabug-at nga elemento sa periodic table!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Elements! They are the simplest substances that combine to make up all the matter in our world.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only introduces elements as the simplest building blocks of matter. It does not describe pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements vs. compounds, or the unique number of protons in an atom, which are the core requirements of G8-M-4. This is useful background knowledge but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
What are the tiniest building blocks that make up everything around us?

Elements! They are the simplest substances that combine to make up all the matter in our world.
copy.tl:
Ano ang mga pinakamaliit na building blocks na bumubuo sa lahat ng bagay sa paligid natin?

Mga elemento! Sila ang pinakasimpleng mga sangkap na bumubuo sa lahat ng matter sa ating mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakagamay nga building blocks nga naglangkob sa tanang butang sa atong palibot?

Mga elemento! Sila ang pinakayano nga mga sangkap nga naglangkob sa tanang matter sa atong kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An atom is the smallest piece of an element that keeps its identity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that an atom is the smallest piece of an element that keeps its identity, but it does not describe the properties of pure substances (fixed chemical composition, elements/compounds) or the unique number of protons per element. It only touches on the atom-element relationship without addressing the specific competency content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An atom is the smallest piece of an element that keeps its identity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the atom but does not describe or draw the structure of an atom in terms of nucleus and electron shells. It provides no information about atomic structure, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What's the tiniest piece of an element that's still that element?

It's the atom! An atom is the smallest piece of an element that keeps its identity. Split it further by chemistry, and it's no longer that element!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamaliit na piraso ng elemento na nananatiling elemento pa rin?

Ang atom! Ito ang pinakamaliit na piraso ng elemento na hindi nawawalan ng pagkaelemento. Hatiin mo pa sa kemikal, hindi na ito ang elementong iyon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakagamay nga piraso sa elemento nga elemento gihapon kini?

Ang atomo! Kini ang pinakagamay nga piraso sa elemento nga wala pa mawala ang pagka-elemento niini. Bahina pa sa kemika, dili na kini kana nga elemento!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The African elephant has much bigger ears than the Asian elephant.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a physical difference between two elephant species but does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention adaptation, mimicry, camouflage, or any environmental pressure. It only provides a trait comparison without linking it to adaptation.

copy.en: The African elephant has much bigger ears than the Asian elephant.
copy.tl: Mas malalaki ang tainga ng elepanteng Aprikano kaysa sa elepanteng Asyano.
copy.bis: Mas dagko ang dalunggan sa elepanteng Aprikano kaysa sa elepanteng Asyano.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The elephant has the heaviest brain of any land animal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a fact about an animal's brain weight; it does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups, nor does it support the skill of classification by similar characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The elephant has the heaviest brain of any land animal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It is only topically related to animals.

copy.en:
Which land animal has the heaviest brain?

The elephant has the heaviest brain of any land animal, weighing about 5 kilograms.
copy.tl:
Aling hayop sa lupa ang may pinakamabigat na utak?

Ang elepante ang may pinakamabigat na utak sa mga hayop sa lupa, halos 5 kilo ang timbang.
copy.bis:
Unsang hayop sa yuta ang adunay pinakabug-at nga utok?

Ang elepante adunay pinakabug-at nga utok sa tanang hayop sa yuta, mga 5 ka kilo ang gibug-aton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Elephants live for about 60 to 70 years in the wild.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the lifespan of elephants. It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, nor describe stages from birth to adulthood, egg to mature organism, or seed to mature plant. Lifespan is not a life-cycle stage comparison.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Elephants live for about 60 to 70 years in the wild.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a living thing (elephant) but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Lifespan is not one of these characteristics, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Elephants live for about 60 to 70 years in the wild.
copy.tl: Ang mga elepante ay nabubuhay nang mga 60 hanggang 70 taon sa kalikasan.
copy.bis: Ang mga elepante mabuhi og mga 60 ngadto sa 70 ka tuig sa ihalas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using just its long trunk, it can lift heavy tree branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the trunk as an outer body part and describes it lifting branches, but the competency requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. Lifting branches is not explicitly tied to movement or food gathering, and the card does not describe the trunk's role in either of those actions. It only states a strength-related function, so it is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support.

copy.en: The elephant is one of the strongest land animals — using just its long trunk, it can lift heavy tree branches.
copy.tl: Ang elepante ang isa sa pinakamalakas na hayop sa lupa. Gamit lang ang mahabang nguso nito, kaya nitong buhatin ang mabibigat na sanga ng puno.
copy.bis: Ang elepante usa sa pinakakusgan nga mga hayop sa yuta. Gamit lang ang taas niini nga nguso, makahimo kini sa pag-alsa sa bug-at nga mga sanga sa kahoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cooked by the steam of boiling water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions boiling water producing steam, which is a change of state, but it does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes. It only describes cooking via steam, not the underlying heat-energy/state-change mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cooked by the steam of boiling water until it firms up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a change in the meat (firming up) due to heat, but the competency specifically targets changes in materials like wood or coal when burned, i.e., combustion-related property changes. Steaming meat is not a comparable example and the card does not describe property changes in the sense of the competency.

copy.en: Embutido is a Filipino meatloaf made of ground pork, cooked by the steam of boiling water until it firms up and is fully cooked!
copy.tl: Ang embutido ay isang Pilipinong meatloaf na gawa sa giniling na baboy, niluluto sa singaw ng kumukulong tubig hanggang tumigas at maluto!
copy.bis: Ang embutido usa ka Pilipinhong meatloaf nga gihimo sa giniling nga baboy, giluto pinaagi sa alisngaw sa nagbukal nga tubig hangtod mogahi ug maluto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: emerald is actually the bright green variety of the mineral beryl
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about emerald being green beryl. It does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting rocks, nor describing similarities and differences in features such as texture, color, or grain crystal size. The content is only tangentially related to the topic of rocks and minerals.

copy.en: A gorgeous emerald is actually the bright green variety of the mineral beryl!
copy.tl: Ang isang magandang emerald ay ang berdeng uri ng mineral na beryl!
copy.bis: Ang usa ka nindot nga emerald mao ang berde nga matang sa mineral nga beryl!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The emu is the second-largest bird in the whole world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about an emu (a bird) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only mentions a bird, which is one of the groups, but provides no classification or comparison of characteristics.

copy.en: The emu is the second-largest bird in the whole world, and it comes all the way from Australia.
copy.tl: Ang emu ang pangalawang pinakamalaking ibon sa buong mundo, at galing ito sa Australia.
copy.bis: Ang emu mao ang ikaduha nga pinakadako nga langgam sa tibuok kalibutan, ug gikan kini sa Australia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Enceladus has a liquid water ocean beneath its thick ice crust. Cassini discovered geysers shooting water and ice particles into space from cracks near the moon's south pole!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific moon of Saturn (Enceladus) and its subsurface ocean and geysers. While this is a celestial object with a main feature and composition, the competency asks students to describe the general structure of the solar system and identify the names of major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition. The card does not address the solar system's structure or place Enceladus within it, and Enceladus is not a major celestial object in the sense of the competency. It shares vocabulary about celestial objects but does not directly teach the stated skill.

copy.en:
Could there be an ocean on Saturn's moon Enceladus?

Yes! Enceladus has a liquid water ocean beneath its thick ice crust. Cassini discovered geysers shooting water and ice particles into space from cracks near the moon's south pole!
copy.tl:
May ocean ba sa buwan ng Saturn na Enceladus?

Oo! May liquid water ocean sa ilalim ng makapal na ice crust ng Enceladus. Natuklasan ng Cassini ang mga geyser na nagpaputok ng tubig at ice particles sa kalawakan mula sa timog polo!
copy.bis:
May ocean ba sa buwan sa Saturn nga Enceladus?

Oo! Adunay liquid water ocean sa ubos sa baga nga ice crust sa Enceladus. Nakakaplag ang Cassini og mga geyser nga nagpuga sa tubig ug ice particles sa kalawakan gikan sa habagatan nga poste!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An endemic species is an animal or plant found in only one place on the whole planet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines endemic species and gives the Philippine eagle as an example, but it does not classify Philippine animals or plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable. Endemism is not conservation status.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: like the Philippine eagle, found only in the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). The format-required representation is absent, and the content is about geographic endemism, not habitat classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An endemic species is an animal or plant found in only one place on the whole planet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: Endemism is loosely connected to isolation in evolution, but the card does not discuss variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation as evolutionary concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An endemic species is an animal or plant found in only one place on the whole planet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines endemism but does not explain how high biodiversity maintains ecosystem stability during food shortages, disease, or climate change.

copy.en:
What does 'endemic species' mean?

An endemic species is an animal or plant found in only one place on the whole planet — like the Philippine eagle, found only in the Philippines.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng 'endemic' na species?

Ang endemic na species ay hayop o halaman na makikita lang sa iisang lugar sa buong mundo — tulad ng Philippine eagle na nasa Pilipinas lang makikita.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa 'endemic' nga species?

Ang endemic nga species usa ka mananap o tanom nga makita lamang sa usa ka lugar sa tibuok kalibutan — sama sa Philippine eagle nga sa Pilipinas ra makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: glands above your kidneys release adrenaline — that's why your heart suddenly pounds and breathing speeds up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a coordinated body response (adrenaline affecting heart and breathing), which is thematically about body systems working together. However, the competency explicitly requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and the card is plain text with no such representation. It also does not address the digestion/excretion example. Thus it is related but not direct.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: getting your body ready to run or fight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a stress response that helps the body react, which touches on maintaining balance for survival. However, it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor mention indicators like body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure. The fight-or-flight response is a homeostatic mechanism, but the card does not teach the competency's core concept.

copy.en:
Why does your heart pound when scared?

When you get scared or startled, glands above your kidneys release adrenaline — that's why your heart suddenly pounds and breathing speeds up, getting your body ready to run or fight!
copy.tl:
Bakit kumakabog ang puso pag natakot?

Kapag natakot o nagulat ka, ang adrenal glands sa itaas ng bato mo ay nagbubuga ng adrenaline — kaya biglang kumakabog ang dibdib at bumibilis ang paghinga, para handa tumakbo o lumaban ang katawan!
copy.bis:
Nganong mokusog ang kasingkasing pag mahadlok?

Kon mahadlok o makalitan ka, ang adrenal glands sa ibabaw sa imong kidney magbuhi og adrenaline — mao nga kalit mokusog ang pitik sa dughan ug mopaspas ang ginhawa, aron andam modagan o makig-away ang lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body releases a hormone called melatonin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific physiological response (melatonin release causing drowsiness) but does not teach the general characteristic of living things responding, nor growth or reproduction. It shares the vocabulary of 'respond' only indirectly.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body releases a hormone called melatonin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a hormone and its effect on sleep, but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and does not explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). It is a single endocrine fact, not a systems-integration lesson.

copy.en:
Why do you feel sleepy at night?

When it gets dark, your body releases a hormone called melatonin that says 'time to sleep'—that's why you feel drowsy. Bright phone light at night can interfere with it.
copy.tl:
Bakit inaantok tayo sa gabi?

Pagdilim, nagbubuga ang katawan ng hormone na melatonin na nagsasabing 'oras nang matulog'—kaya inaantok tayo. Ang sobrang ilaw ng cellphone sa gabi ay puwedeng makasagabal dito.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga katulgon kita sa gabii?

Pagngitngit, magbuhi ang lawas og hormone nga melatonin nga nag-ingon 'panahon na matulog'—mao nga katulgon kita. Ang sobra ka hayag nga suga sa cellphone sa gabii makababag niini.
